quote_text:
David, your take on the game? Didn’t think it  was a great game from either side. I think the  
heat might have played a little bit. It was  a warm day, probably the first of the year,  
just about. But I didn’t think we deserved to  come away with no points in the game. Yeah,  
that was about it really. Game felt in the balance  at half-time. How much of a blow was it to concede  
so soon after? Yeah, we didn’t start the  opening of the second half particularly well,  
but we played much better probably the second part  of the second half and got a goal back and could  
have maybe had another one. So we looked at that  time as if we were the better team. But obviously  
West Ham getting the goal gave them something  to defend, something to hold on to, and we got  
the goal back and I thought it was deserved  at that time. Truly disappointing. And just  
on the handball? Yeah, I do. I think it would be  still pretty harsh on Fernandes, but he certainly  
punches the ball out. He puts his arms round and  it’s not as if the ball comes onto his hand. His  
arm goes towards the ball. And I think today’s the  first time I’ve heard the word accidental being  
used, which I don’t think. I think that word had  been taken out the vocabulary really, because I  
don’t think anybody’s used that word in the whole  season really on handball situations. Any further  
questions? Tell us how important Tomáš Souček was  to you? Bloody hell. He’s great. Does great. He’s  
done brilliant for West Ham and I think he’s come  in for a little bit maybe over certain times, but  
his worth has been enormous because of his goals.  The type of boy he is, everything about him,  
he epitomises a lot of things that you want as  a coach. Somebody who’s willing to work hard and  
does a lot of the unselfish jobs for the team.  He heads the ball in both boxes quite regular.  
So he’s been a big player for West Ham. I think  the goal, the first goal today, was quite similar,  
probably similar zone to the Van Dijk one  a week ago. Absolutely. How concerning is  
it? Is that something? It’s not something very,  very concerning. I mean, I think we were probably  
third best defensive record at set pieces or  something before coming into today’s game.  
But no, two goals were too similar for my liking.  Do you think in terms of both of those goals, it  
shows the value of Beto and Branthwaite? They’ve  got big physical presences that have that impact.  
Well, I think what it is, is it tells you if  you’re going to try and be successful in the  
Premier League, you’re going to need physical  stature in places. And sometimes you’re having  
to play players because of that, requiring that  to be able to accommodate not conceding goals,  
maybe helping you score goals. And let’s be fair  today, Tomáš Souček might not be the first pick  
as a technical football player, but because he can  score and because he can head out the other box,  
it becomes really important in the team setup.  So that’s why trying to get the balance right  
between that type of player and smaller, maybe  more technical players. We’re just having a bit  
of a difficult time in the last two games with  it. All right, folks. Sorry. I think West Ham  
have got momentum, and I think momentum  in the Premier League is, at this moment,  
the way the league’s going, you need to sort of  keep it going. I mean, today we’ve come in with  
a brilliant away record, so we’ve not lost too  many games away from home in the Premier League,  
and it didn’t look we would do that today.  But I think West Ham have got a wee bit of  
momentum going and it’ll help them if they keep it  going. Thank you very much. Thank you. Yeah. No,  
don’t think there was any birthday happening  today, that’s for sure. No, no. Okay, cheers.
title: MOYES: “SOUCEK’S WORTH HAS BEEN ENORMOUS!”  West Ham 2-1 Everton
